answer_1.quote: To take advantage of the advanced contextual understanding capability and internal knowledge of ChatGPT to inject discourse knowledge, we design a prompt that allows ChatGPT to paraphrase the sample x_n, supplementing its acronyms, hashtags, slang, and references, and yielding the knowledge integrated sample D_n ... We build the prompt as: USER: Sentence: x_n . Target: t_n . Wikipedia Document: W_i . If ... summarize the knowledge from the document which related to the given [Sentence] and the given [Target].
answer_1.outputs: Generated episodic knowledge (summaries of Wikipedia documents) and discourse knowledge (paraphrased text with expanded acronyms/hashtags) that are concatenated with the original tweet for stance classification.

answer_4.quote: We randomly select 500 samples from the Sem16, P-Stance, Covid19, and VAST datasets and use human evaluation (with three evaluators who are not involved in this work) to measure the quality of the data generated by ChatGPT.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators answer "yes" or "no" to three questions: (1) whether the filtered episodic knowledge is relevant to the sample; (2) whether the filtered redundant content does not contain the required episodic knowledge; (3) whether the generated discourse knowledge is consistent with the original content.
criteria: consistency of discourse knowledge with original text
